pages.title: Publication Ethics and Malpractice Statement
pages.html:
The Journal of Contemporary Eastern Asia (JCEA) is a member of the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) and follows the COPE Core Practices and flowcharts in handling every matter described on this page. The journal also follows the CONSORT and TOP (Transparency and Openness Promotion) guidelines and the ACOMS editorial standards.

Editorial responsibility for these policies rests with the Editor-in-Chief. Questions and reports may be sent to j.c.eastern.asia@gmail.com.

On this page

  • Authorship and contributorship
  • Complaints and appeals
  • Allegations of research misconduct
  • Conflicts of interest
  • Data sharing and reproducibility
  • Ethical oversight
  • Intellectual property and research integrity
  • Post-publication discussion
  • Corrections, retractions and expressions of concern
  • Use of generative AI

Authorship and contributorship

JCEA applies authorship criteria consistent with the ICMJE recommendations. Authorship is limited to those who have made a substantial intellectual contribution to the work. Each named author must satisfy all four of the following:

  1. substantial contribution to the conception or design of the work, or to the acquisition, analysis or interpretation of the data;
  2. drafting the manuscript or revising it critically for important intellectual content;
  3. final approval of the version submitted for publication; and
  4. agreement to be accountable for all aspects of the work, including the accuracy and integrity of any part of it.

Contributors who do not meet all four criteria — for example those who provided funding, general supervision, data collection alone, or language assistance — should be named in the acknowledgements rather than listed as authors. Guest, gift and ghost authorship are not permitted.

The corresponding author submits on behalf of all co-authors and warrants that every author has seen and approved the submission. Any change to the author list after submission — addition, removal, or change of order — requires a signed request from all authors, including the author being added or removed, stating the reason for the change. Requests must reach the editorial office before publication; after publication a change to the author list is handled as a correction (see below).

Authors are encouraged to include a contributorship statement describing each author's role, and to supply ORCID identifiers.

Complaints and appeals

Appeals against editorial decisions. An author who believes a decision was based on a material misunderstanding of the manuscript, or on a review that was factually incorrect, may appeal once. Appeals are sent to j.c.eastern.asia@gmail.com with the subject line “Appeal” and must set out the specific points at issue and the author's response to each. Disagreement with a reviewer's judgement of significance or fit is not in itself grounds for appeal.

Appeals are considered by the Editor-in-Chief, or, where the Editor-in-Chief handled the original decision or has any conflicting interest, by a Managing Editor who was not involved. The editorial office aims to acknowledge an appeal within one week and to communicate an outcome within eight weeks. The decision on an appeal is final. Manuscripts under appeal should not be submitted elsewhere until the appeal has concluded.

Complaints about the journal. Complaints about editorial process, conduct of staff, editors or reviewers, or about the handling of an ethical matter should be sent to the same address and will be answered by the Editor-in-Chief. Complaints are logged, investigated, and answered in writing. If the complainant is not satisfied with the outcome, the complaint may be escalated to the publishers — the Cyber Emotions Research Center at Yeungnam University and WATEF — and, where it concerns adherence to publication ethics, to COPE.

Allegations of research misconduct

JCEA takes seriously any allegation of misconduct in a submitted or published article, including plagiarism, self-plagiarism and redundant publication, data fabrication or falsification, image manipulation, citation manipulation, undisclosed conflicts of interest, and breaches of research-ethics requirements.

Allegations may be made by anyone, are treated confidentially, and are assessed on the evidence rather than on the identity or motive of the person raising them. The journal follows the relevant COPE flowchart in every case. In outline:

  1. The editorial office acknowledges the allegation and gathers the documentary evidence.
  2. The corresponding author is informed of the specific concern and invited to respond, normally within four weeks, on behalf of all authors.
  3. Where the response does not resolve the concern, the journal contacts the authors' institution or research-integrity office, which is the appropriate body to conduct a formal investigation. JCEA does not itself adjudicate findings of misconduct.
  4. Consideration of the manuscript is suspended, or an expression of concern is published for an article already in the literature, while an investigation is under way.

Depending on the outcome, the journal may reject the manuscript, require correction, publish a correction or retraction, notify the authors' institution and funder, and decline to consider further submissions from the authors concerned. Neither this policy nor any editorial statement of the journal should be read as encouraging or tolerating misconduct of any kind.

Conflicts of interest

Authors must disclose all financial and non-financial interests that a reasonable reader might consider relevant — funding and grants, employment and consultancies, honoraria, patents and holdings, and personal, political or institutional relationships bearing on the subject of the article. Disclosure is made in the manuscript in a “Conflicts of interest” statement and in the cover letter. Where there are no such interests, the manuscript should state that none exist. Funding sources are named in a funding statement; declaring a funder does not entitle the funder to any influence over the content or the decision.

Reviewers must decline an invitation, or declare the interest and let the editor decide, where they are employed at the same institution as any author, have supervised or been supervised by an author within the past three years, have co-authored or actively collaborated with an author within the past five years, have a close personal relationship with an author, or have any financial interest in the outcome. Every review submitted to JCEA carries a conflict-of-interest declaration.

Editors take no part in decisions on manuscripts they have authored or co-authored, that come from their own institution or from close collaborators, or in which they have any competing interest. Such manuscripts are reassigned to an editor with no connection to the work, and the handling editor's identity is not disclosed to the conflicted editor. Submissions from the Editor-in-Chief are handled in full by a Managing Editor.

Data sharing and reproducibility

JCEA follows the TOP guidelines and encourages open research practice. Authors are encouraged to deposit the data, code and materials underlying their findings in a trusted public repository, and to cite the deposit with a persistent identifier in a “Data availability” statement in the manuscript. Where data cannot be shared — because of participant confidentiality, third-party licensing, or legal restriction — the statement should say so and explain the conditions under which the data may be obtained.

Data sharing is encouraged but not, at present, a condition of publication. Authors are expected to retain their primary data for at least five years after publication and to make it available to the editors on reasonable request where a question about the findings arises.

Ethical oversight

Research involving human participants — including surveys, interviews, experiments and the collection or analysis of identifiable social-media data — must have been conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki and with the requirements of the authors' institutions. Manuscripts reporting such research must state the name of the approving research-ethics committee or institutional review board and the approval reference, or, where formal approval was not required, explain why. Manuscripts must state that informed consent was obtained from participants, and that consent to publish was obtained where individuals could be identified.

Authors working with vulnerable populations, sensitive political material, or data obtained from online platforms are expected to describe the steps taken to protect participants from harm and to safeguard anonymity. Editors may request evidence of ethical approval at any stage and may decline a manuscript on ethical grounds regardless of its scholarly quality.

Intellectual property and research integrity

Manuscripts must be original, must not have been published previously, and must not be under consideration elsewhere. Prior appearance as a conference abstract, a thesis chapter, or a preprint does not preclude submission, but must be disclosed in the cover letter with a link to the earlier version. Publication of substantially the same work in more than one journal (redundant or duplicate publication), and the division of a single study into multiple minimally distinct articles, are not acceptable.

All submissions are screened for textual overlap. Authors are required to supply an originality report from an international plagiarism-detection service with their submission, and the journal screens suspected cases with iThenticate. Plagiarism of text, data, images or ideas, in any proportion and from any source including the authors' own earlier work, is a ground for rejection or retraction.

Citation manipulation — adding citations whose primary purpose is to increase the citation count of an author, a colleague or this journal — is not permitted. Reviewers and editors must not require authors to cite their own work or work published in JCEA as a condition of acceptance. Falsification or fabrication of data, and the manipulation of images beyond adjustments that leave the original information intact, are treated as misconduct.

Authors must hold the rights to all material they submit and must obtain and evidence written permission for the reproduction of copyrighted figures, tables, extended quotations or datasets. Copyright in JCEA articles remains with the authors; see Copyright and Licence.

Post-publication discussion

Scholarly debate about work published in JCEA is welcome. Readers who wish to comment on, question or dispute a published article may write to j.c.eastern.asia@gmail.com. Substantive commentaries are sent to the authors of the original article for response and, where the editors judge that the exchange advances the field, both the commentary and the response may be published in a subsequent issue, subject to editorial review. Comments raising an integrity concern are handled under the misconduct policy above rather than as scholarly debate.

The journal does not host an on-site comment facility. Published articles carry a DOI so that post-publication discussion elsewhere can cite them unambiguously.

Corrections, retractions and expressions of concern

The version of record is permanent. JCEA does not remove published articles from the record; errors are addressed by publishing a linked notice, following the COPE retraction guidelines.

  • Correction (erratum / corrigendum). Where an error affects the record but not the reliability of the findings — an incorrect figure, a mislabelled table, a missing funding disclosure, an author-list error — a correction notice is published in the next issue. The notice states what was wrong and what is correct, is linked from the original article, and is itself citable.
  • Retraction. Where the findings are unreliable, whether through honest error or misconduct; where the work has been published elsewhere; where material has been plagiarised; or where the research was carried out without required ethical approval, the article is retracted. The article remains online, is clearly marked as retracted on the landing page and in the full text, and retains its original DOI. The retraction notice names the reason, states who is retracting the article, and is linked from the original.
  • Expression of concern. Where a serious concern has been raised that cannot yet be resolved — for example while an institutional investigation is under way, or where an investigation has not been conducted fairly — the editors may publish an expression of concern, linked from the article, and update or replace it once the matter is resolved.

Retraction and correction notices are free to read, are indexed, and are sent to the databases and indexing services that carry the journal. Requests for a correction or retraction may be made by the authors or by any reader, and are assessed by the Editor-in-Chief.

Use of generative AI

Authors. Generative AI tools cannot be listed as an author: authorship carries accountability that only a person can hold. Authors who have used generative AI in the preparation of a manuscript — for drafting, translating, editing, coding, analysing or generating figures — must disclose the tool, the version, and how it was used, in the methods section or the acknowledgements. Language polishing by an AI tool should be disclosed but does not require description in the methods. Authors remain fully responsible for the accuracy, originality and integrity of everything they submit, including any citation or quotation produced by such a tool.

Reviewers and editors. Manuscripts under review are confidential. Reviewers and editors must not upload a manuscript, or any part of one, to a generative AI service that does not guarantee confidentiality, and must not delegate their judgement to such a tool. A review must be the reviewer's own assessment.

The journal. JCEA publishes optional AI-generated companion material — plain-language summaries, audio summaries and visualisations — only where the authors have given explicit opt-in consent and an editor has approved the output. Companion material is labelled as AI-generated wherever it appears, and the peer-reviewed article remains the authoritative version of the work.

Related: Editorial Process and Peer Review · Copyright and Licence · Author Fees and Business Model · Archiving and Digital Preservation

pages.title: Archiving and Digital Preservation
pages.html:
Everything JCEA publishes is intended to remain permanently available, whether or not the journal, its publishers or its current hosts continue to operate. This page sets out how that is achieved.

Long-term digital preservation

The full content of the Journal of Contemporary Eastern Asia is deposited with and preserved by NDSL, the national scholarly-information service operated by the Korea Institute of Science and Technology Information (KISTI), a government research institute of the Republic of Korea. KISTI maintains the archive independently of the journal and of its publishers, so the content survives the failure of either. The journal's preservation record is registered with the Directory of Open Access Journals.

The archived record covers the complete run of the journal, including back content published before the current publishers took over in 2012.

Hosting of the version of record

The full text of every article is hosted on KoreaScience, the open-access platform operated by KISTI, which serves the PDF version of record. This journal website, a separate service hosted and maintained by Boston-based AI scholarly agents, provides the article landing pages, metadata, abstracts and citation export, and links to the full text on KoreaScience. Content is therefore available from more than one independently operated system at all times.

Persistent identifiers

Every article is registered with a DOI under the journal's prefix 10.17477. A DOI resolves to the current location of the article regardless of which platform hosts it, so citations remain valid if hosting arrangements change. Article metadata, including the DOI, author list, affiliations, abstract, and licence, is deposited with the DOI registration agency and distributed to indexing services.

If the journal ceases to publish

Should the Journal of Contemporary Eastern Asia cease publication, or should its publishers cease to operate, the published content will remain accessible through the NDSL/KISTI archive and KoreaScience under the same open-access terms, and the registered DOIs will continue to resolve. No article will be withdrawn from the record as a consequence of the journal ceasing to publish. The publishers undertake to transfer the archive to another recognised preservation service if the present arrangement can no longer be maintained.

Self-archiving by authors

Authors may deposit their articles in institutional and subject repositories without embargo. The conditions are set out on the Copyright and Licence page.

Corrections to the archived record

Published articles are never silently altered or deleted. Errors and integrity problems are addressed by publishing linked correction, retraction or expression-of-concern notices, as described in the Publication Ethics policy; the original article remains in place with its original DOI.

Related: Abstracting, Indexing and Preservation · Copyright and Licence · Publication Ethics

pages.title: Author Fees, Waivers and Business Model
pages.html:
JCEA is a fully open-access journal. Readers pay nothing, and there is no subscription of any kind. Publication is funded by institutional support from the journal's publishers and by an article processing charge payable by authors on acceptance.

Submission fees

There is no submission fee. No charge of any kind is made for submitting a manuscript, for peer review, or for a manuscript that is rejected.

Article processing charge (APC)

An article processing charge becomes payable only after a manuscript has been accepted for publication.

ManuscriptCharge
Accepted article, research not externally fundedUSD 100 (KRW 150,000)
Accepted article reporting externally funded researchUSD 300 (KRW 450,000) in total — the USD 100 base charge plus a USD 200 (KRW 300,000) supplement

The charge covers editorial handling, copy-editing, XML conversion and typesetting, DOI registration, hosting and long-term preservation. It is invoiced by the editorial office after acceptance and before production. Research is treated as externally funded where a grant, contract or institutional publication fund is acknowledged in the article.

Other charges

Where an accepted manuscript requires substantial language editing beyond normal copy-editing, the journal will inform the corresponding author of the additional cost and obtain the author's agreement before that work is commissioned. No other charge is made: there are no page charges, colour charges, or charges for supplementary material.

Waivers and exemptions

The following exemptions apply and are stated here so that authors can establish their position before submitting:

  • Associate Editors of JCEA are exempt from the article processing charge for up to one unfunded publication per calendar year.
  • Scholars publishing at the invitation of the editors — invited articles, editor's notes and commissioned contributions — are exempt.

Authors who face genuine difficulty in meeting the charge should write to the editorial office at j.c.eastern.asia@gmail.com before submitting, explaining the circumstances. Requests are decided by the Editor-in-Chief. Eligibility rests with the corresponding author, who applies on behalf of all authors; a request cannot be made after acceptance, and no request is disclosed to reviewers or to the handling editor.

Neither the ability to pay an article processing charge, nor the existence of a waiver request or exemption, plays any part in editorial decision making. Editors and reviewers assess manuscripts on scholarly merit alone and are not told the fee or waiver status of a submission. Charges are raised only after a decision to accept has been taken.

Sources of revenue

JCEA is funded from two sources:

  • Institutional support from the journal's publishers, the Cyber Emotions Research Center at Yeungnam University (Republic of Korea) and WATEF, the World Association for Triple Helix and Future Strategy Studies, which meet the journal's editorial and platform costs; and
  • Article processing charges as set out above.

The journal receives no subscription, licensing, reprint or supplement revenue, and does not publish sponsored issues or sponsored articles. No source of revenue and no sponsoring body influences editorial decision making. Editorial responsibility rests with the Editor-in-Chief and the editorial team, who take decisions independently of the publishers and of any funder of the research under consideration.

Advertising

JCEA does not accept advertising. No advertisement appears on this website, in any issue, or in any article, and the journal does not sell advertising space to any party. Should this ever change, an advertising policy stating the types of advertisement accepted, who decides on acceptance, and how advertisements are separated from published content will be published on this page before any advertisement appears.

Direct marketing

The journal's direct marketing is limited to calls for papers and issue announcements, sent to authors who have previously published in or reviewed for JCEA, to members of its editorial board, and to delegates of conferences with which the journal is associated. Such messages identify the journal and its publishers accurately, describe the journal's scope, standards and charges truthfully, make no claim about impact, indexing or acceptance that is not verifiable on this website, and offer an unsubscribe route. JCEA does not carry out mass unsolicited solicitation of manuscripts, and does not engage third parties to solicit on its behalf.

Email addresses entered on this site are used only for the stated purposes of the journal and are not supplied to any third party.

Related: Submission Guidelines · About the Journal · Publication Ethics

pages.title: Editorial Process and Peer Review
pages.html:
All research published in the Journal of Contemporary Eastern Asia is peer reviewed. Reviews are carried out by external experts in the field — not by the handling editor alone and not, as a matter of course, by members of the editorial board. This page describes the review model, who takes each decision, and how long each stage should take.

Type of peer review

JCEA operates single-anonymised peer review: the identities of the reviewers are not disclosed to the authors, while the reviewers see the authors' identities. Certain special issues are handled double-anonymised at the discretion of the guest editors, in which case the call for papers for that issue says so and authors are asked to supply an anonymised manuscript file.

Reviews are not published alongside articles and reviewers are not asked to sign their reports. Reviewer identities remain confidential indefinitely, unless a reviewer asks the editor to disclose their identity to the authors and the editor agrees.

Supplementary material submitted with a manuscript is provided to reviewers and is assessed as part of the article; it is not separately peer reviewed after acceptance and is published as supplied by the authors.

What is peer reviewed, and what is not

  • Full-length research articles and short research papers / rapid communications are peer reviewed by at least two external reviewers.
  • Book reviews and editor's notes are not sent for external peer review. They are assessed editorially by the Book Review Editor or the Editor-in-Chief for accuracy, fairness and fit, and are labelled as such on their article pages so that readers can distinguish them from peer-reviewed research.

No manuscript is accepted without evaluation. Acceptance is never guaranteed by submission, by payment of any charge, or by invitation to submit.

The process, stage by stage

1. Pre-check

A Managing Editor screens each submission for scope and fit, completeness against the submission checklist, compliance with the manuscript template and word limits, and evidence of originality screening. Manuscripts that fall outside the journal's scope, that do not meet its basic standards, or that do not comply with the format requirements are declined at this stage without external review, normally within two weeks. The Editor-in-Chief or, for a special issue, the Guest Editor is then notified and proposes reviewers.

2. Peer review

At least two independent review reports are obtained for every research article. Reviewers are selected for their published expertise in the subject of the manuscript. A reviewer must:

  • have no conflict of interest with any author (see the conflicts of interest policy) — in particular, reviewers are not selected from an author's own institution, from among an author's supervisors or students within the past three years, or from among co-authors and active collaborators within the past five years;
  • hold a doctorate, save in fields where an equivalent professional standing is customary;
  • have recent publications in the subject area of the manuscript; and
  • not have reviewed for the journal in the immediately preceding period, so that the reviewer pool is not concentrated in a few hands.

Every reviewer completes a conflict-of-interest declaration before submitting a report. Reviewers are asked to treat the manuscript as confidential, not to use its content for their own purposes, and not to upload it to any generative AI service (see the AI policy).

Author-recommended reviewers. Authors are asked at submission to suggest three experts in their area, with affiliations and a short rationale for each. Suggestions must not include co-authors, colleagues at the author's own institution, supervisors or students. The editors are not bound by these suggestions; they are one input among several, and the editors routinely identify reviewers independently. A decision is never based solely on reports from author-recommended reviewers. Authors may also name individuals they would prefer not to review the manuscript, with reasons; the editors will normally respect such a request but are not obliged to.

3. Editorial decision

The handling editor assesses the suitability of the reviewers, the adequacy and consistency of their reports, and the scientific quality of the manuscript, and recommends one of: accept, reject, revise (minor or major), or seek a further review. Where two reports conflict materially, a third reviewer is invited.

The Editor-in-Chief is responsible for the academic quality of the publication process and takes the final decision on every manuscript, or delegates that authority to a Managing Editor or, for a special issue, to a Guest Editor. Reviewers advise; they do not decide. Where the Editor-in-Chief is an author of the manuscript, is at the same institution as an author, or has any other competing interest, the manuscript is handled in full by a Managing Editor with no connection to the work.

4. Revision

Authors invited to revise receive the full text of the reviewers' comments and are asked to return a revised manuscript together with a point-by-point response. Revised manuscripts are normally returned to the original reviewers. A manuscript will not go through more than two rounds of major revision other than in exceptional circumstances; an invitation to revise is not a commitment to publish.

5. Production

Accepted manuscripts are copy-edited, professionally language-edited where required, converted to XML, and typeset. Proofs are sent to the corresponding author for approval. The article is then registered with a DOI, published in the next issue, and deposited for indexing and preservation. Where substantial language editing is required, the cost is disclosed to the author in advance — see Author Fees.

Timelines

StageTarget
Pre-check decision2 weeks from submission
Reviewer report on a new manuscript2 weeks from acceptance of the invitation
Reviewer report on a revised manuscript3 days
Submission to first decisionapproximately 2 months
Submission to publication (journal average, as recorded with DOAJ)approximately 14 weeks

These are targets and a published average, not guarantees. Where a manuscript is delayed beyond them — most often because a reviewer withdraws late and a replacement must be found — the editorial office informs the corresponding author of the reason and the expected timetable. An author whose manuscript is delayed may withdraw it at any time, without charge, by writing to j.c.eastern.asia@gmail.com.

Publication dates

Every article carries its date of publication on the article page. Articles published from 2026 onwards also carry the dates on which the manuscript was received and accepted.

Integrity screening

Authors must supply an originality report from an international plagiarism-detection service with their submission. In addition, the editorial office screens manuscripts with iThenticate where overlap is suspected at any stage, including after acceptance. Suspected plagiarism, redundant publication, data fabrication or falsification, image manipulation and citation manipulation are handled under the journal's research misconduct policy.

Ethics and standards

JCEA is a member of the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) and follows its Core Practices and flowcharts, together with the CONSORT, TOP and ACOMS guidelines. Appeals against decisions and complaints about the editorial process are handled as described under Complaints and appeals.

Related: Publication Ethics · Submission Guidelines · Editorial Board

pages.title: Copyright and Licence
pages.html:
Authors keep the copyright in their articles. Every article in the Journal of Contemporary Eastern Asia is published open access under a Creative Commons licence, free to read and to redistribute with attribution.

Article licence

All articles are published under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International licence (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0). The licence is stated on every article landing page and on the full text.

Under this licence anyone may:

  • copy and redistribute the article in any medium or format, in print or electronically,

provided that:

  • Attribution — appropriate credit is given to the author(s), a link to the licence is provided, and the article's original publication in JCEA is acknowledged;
  • NonCommercial — the material is not used for commercial purposes; and
  • NoDerivatives — if the material is remixed, transformed or built upon, the modified material may not be distributed.

Rights that are not restricted by the licence are unaffected: fair dealing and fair use, quotation, and the author's moral rights all remain. The copyright holder may grant permission for any use outside the licence terms; requests should be addressed to the corresponding author, with a copy to the editorial office.

Articles published before this policy took effect were issued under earlier versions of the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivs licence. The licence stated on each article page is the licence that applies to that article.

Copyright in articles

Authors retain copyright in their work. On acceptance, authors grant the journal the right of first publication and a non-exclusive licence to publish, distribute, index and archive the article under the terms above. There is no transfer of copyright to the journal or to its publishers. The copyright holder — the author or authors — is named on every article, on the article landing page and on the full text.

Copyright in this website

Copyright in this website — its design, navigation, editorial pages and compilation — belongs to the Journal of Contemporary Eastern Asia and its publishers, the Cyber Emotions Research Center at Yeungnam University and WATEF, and is separate from the copyright in the articles. Website material outside the articles is not covered by the article licence and may not be reproduced without permission.

Self-archiving and repository deposit

Authors may deposit their work in repositories without asking permission and without any embargo:

  • the submitted version (preprint) may be posted at any time, on a preprint server, a personal or institutional website, or a subject repository;
  • the accepted manuscript may be deposited in an institutional or subject repository, or a funder's repository, immediately on acceptance; and
  • the published version of record may be deposited in an institutional or subject repository, posted on the author's own or their institution's website, and included in a thesis or a book by the author, immediately on publication.

Every deposit must acknowledge first publication in the Journal of Contemporary Eastern Asia, cite the article's DOI, link to the version of record, and state the CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 licence. Authors are welcome, though not required, to notify the editorial office of a deposit or a reproduction at j.c.eastern.asia@gmail.com.

Authors may also enter into separate, non-exclusive arrangements for the distribution of the published version — for instance publication in an edited collection — on the same conditions.

Third-party material

Where an article reproduces figures, tables, images, extended quotations or datasets in which copyright is held by someone else, the authors are responsible for obtaining written permission before submission and for supplying the required credit line. Third-party material remains under its own terms and is not covered by the article's Creative Commons licence; where this is the case it is marked in the article.

Open access

JCEA is a fully open-access journal. All content is freely available to readers and their institutions from the moment of publication. Readers may read, download, copy, distribute, print, search and link to the full text of articles without asking prior permission from the publisher or the author, subject only to the licence terms above. There is no subscription, registration requirement, or pay-per-view charge of any kind, and there is no offline or print edition sold separately. Publication is funded as described under Author Fees and Business Model.

Privacy and jurisdiction

Names and email addresses entered on this site are used exclusively for the stated purposes of this journal and are not made available for any other purpose or to any third party. The court of jurisdiction is Daegu, Republic of Korea.

Related: Publication Ethics · Archiving and Digital Preservation · Author Fees and Business Model

pages.title: Submission Guidelines
pages.html:
The Journal of Contemporary Eastern Asia welcomes original research on political, social and economic trends in East and Southeast Asia, and on socio-technical convergence and future network studies. Before submitting, please read the Publication Ethics policy and the fee and waiver policy.

How to submit

Manuscripts are submitted through the ACOMS+ system at acoms.accesson.kr/jceasia. For technical problems with the submission system, contact acomsplus@kisti.re.kr. For questions about the editorial process, contact the editorial office at j.c.eastern.asia@gmail.com.

Fees

There is no submission fee. An article processing charge of USD 100 (KRW 150,000) is payable on acceptance, or USD 300 (KRW 450,000) in total where the research was externally funded. Exemptions and waivers, other possible charges, and the journal's business model are set out in full on the Author Fees, Waivers and Business Model page. Fee status plays no part in editorial decisions.

Manuscript types and word limits

TypeLengthPeer reviewed
Full-length original research paperup to 8,000 words including abstract and bibliographyYes — at least two external reviewers
Short research paper / rapid communication2,000–3,000 words including abstract and bibliographyYes — at least two external reviewers
Book reviewup to 5,000 wordsEditorially assessed
Editor's note3–10 pagesEditorially assessed

Special issues carry full-length papers only, normally up to five per issue. See the special issue guidelines (PDF).

Originality and redundant publication

By submitting, the authors confirm that the manuscript is original, that it has not been published before in whole or in substantial part, and that it is not under consideration by another journal. Previous appearance as a conference abstract, a thesis chapter or a preprint does not prevent submission, but must be disclosed in the cover letter with a citation or link to the earlier version.

Publishing substantially the same work in more than one journal, and dividing a single study into several minimally distinct articles, are not acceptable. Where an article draws on the authors' own earlier work, that work must be cited and the overlap explained. See the intellectual property and research integrity policy.

Authorship

Every named author must meet all four of the journal's authorship criteria — substantial contribution, drafting or critical revision, approval of the submitted version, and accountability for the work. Contributors who do not meet all four should be acknowledged instead. Changes to the author list after submission require the written agreement of all authors, including any author being added or removed. To request a change of authorship for an accepted manuscript before publication, complete and return the Request for Authorship Change form (Word). The full policy, including the treatment of guest, gift and ghost authorship, is set out under Authorship and contributorship.

Originality screening

Every submission must be accompanied by a plagiarism check report from Grammarly, Turnitin or another international plagiarism checker. Software designed for Korean-language texts, including CopyKiller, is not accepted for this purpose. The editorial office additionally screens manuscripts with iThenticate where overlap is suspected, at any stage including after acceptance.

Disclosures required in the manuscript

  • Conflicts of interest — all financial and non-financial competing interests of every author, or an explicit statement that there are none.
  • Funding — every grant, contract or publication fund supporting the work, with award numbers where applicable.
  • Ethical approval — for research involving human participants, the approving committee and reference number, and confirmation that informed consent was obtained; or an explanation of why approval was not required.
  • Data availability — where the data, code and materials underlying the findings can be obtained, with a persistent identifier where they are deposited; or the reason they cannot be shared.
  • Use of generative AI — the tool, version and purpose, where such a tool was used in preparing the manuscript. AI tools cannot be named as authors and authors remain fully responsible for the content. See the AI policy.

Format requirements

Manuscripts must be submitted in MS Word or RTF format and must follow the journal's manuscript template. Manuscripts that do not comply with the template and the word limits are returned or declined at pre-check without review.

Pre-submission checklist

  • File is in MS Word or RTF and follows the journal template.
  • The manuscript is within the word limit for its type.
  • Previously published material is properly cited and written permission has been obtained for any copyrighted material reproduced.
  • The cover letter gives the names and contact details of all authors, summarises the research, states that the work is original and not under consideration elsewhere, and discloses any prior posting.
  • The cover letter names three suggested experts in the area, with affiliations and the reason for each recommendation. Suggested reviewers must not be co-authors, colleagues at the same institution, or the authors' supervisors or students. The editors are not bound by these suggestions.
  • A plagiarism check report is attached.
  • Conflict of interest, funding, ethical approval, data availability and AI-use statements are included in the manuscript.

Copyright and licensing

Authors retain copyright and grant the journal the right of first publication. Articles are published under the CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 licence, and authors may deposit the submitted, accepted or published version in a repository without embargo. See Copyright and Licence for the full terms.

Review and timelines

Manuscripts are peer reviewed as described under Editorial Process and Peer Review. Submission to first decision takes approximately two months, and submission to publication approximately fourteen weeks on average. Acceptance is never guaranteed. Authors may withdraw a manuscript at any time, without charge.

Related: Editorial Process and Peer Review · Publication Ethics · Author Fees · Copyright and Licence

pages.title: About the Journal
pages.html:
The Journal of Contemporary Eastern Asia (JCEA) is a peer-reviewed, fully open-access journal on convergence and future studies in Asia. eISSN 2383-9449.

Aims and scope

JCEA publishes peer-reviewed scholarship on East Asia, data, and the networked society. The journal was founded to examine current political, social and economic trends in East and Southeast Asia, and its scope has since broadened to emphasise (socio-technical) convergence and future (network) studies — among them triple-helix and innovation-system research, social network analysis, internet and social-media research, digital culture, science and technology policy, and the social consequences of artificial intelligence in the region.

The journal welcomes articles reporting original empirical or theoretical research, and articles that substantially re-examine an existing body of scholarship. Contributions from any disciplinary background are considered provided the work is methodologically sound and addresses the journal's regional and thematic scope. The manuscript types accepted, and the policy on redundant publication, are set out in the Submission Guidelines.

Target readership

JCEA is written for an international scholarly readership: researchers and graduate students in Asian studies, communication and media studies, political science, sociology, science and technology studies, and innovation policy, together with policy analysts and practitioners working on East and Southeast Asia. Articles are expected to be intelligible to specialists outside the author's own subfield.

Publishing schedule

JCEA publishes two issues a year, in June and December. The journal keeps to this schedule other than in exceptional circumstances, and any change is announced on this website. Articles are published in a numbered issue with continuous pagination; there is no rolling advance publication.

Open access

JCEA is a fully open-access journal. All content is freely available without charge to the reader or the reader's institution from the moment of publication. Users are allowed to read, download, copy, distribute, print, search and link to the full text of articles without prior permission, subject to the terms of the CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 licence under which articles are published. Authors retain copyright. There is no subscription, no registration requirement and no pay-per-view charge.

Publication is funded by institutional support from the journal's publishers together with an article processing charge payable by authors on acceptance — no submission fee, USD 100 (KRW 150,000) on acceptance, or USD 300 (KRW 450,000) where the research was externally funded. Full details, including exemptions, other possible charges and the journal's sources of revenue, are on the Author Fees, Waivers and Business Model page.

Peer review

All research articles are peer reviewed by at least two external experts under a single-anonymised model; book reviews and editor's notes are editorially assessed and are labelled as such. The Editor-in-Chief takes the final decision on every manuscript. The full process, the reviewer-selection criteria and the journal's timelines are described under Editorial Process and Peer Review.

Ownership and management

JCEA is owned and published jointly by two bodies:

  • the Cyber Emotions Research Center at Yeungnam University, Gyeongsan, Republic of Korea, which hosts the editorial office and provides the journal's editorial and administrative support; and
  • WATEF, the World Association for Triple Helix and Future Strategy Studies, the learned society with which the journal is affiliated, which provides its scholarly community and governs the editorial board.

The two bodies share responsibility for the journal under a standing agreement; neither has any role in decisions on individual manuscripts. Editorial authority rests with the Editor-in-Chief and the editorial team, who act independently of the publishers, of the editorial board, and of any funder of the research under consideration. Neither publisher trades under a name that could be confused with any other journal or organisation.

History

The journal was founded in 2001 by the Austrian Association of East Asian Studies, together with scholars from Japan, Taiwan and South Korea, and has been open access since 2002. In 2010 the Cyber Emotions Research Center at Yeungnam University became a co-publisher. Following the closure of the Austrian association in 2012, the journal transferred to the Cyber Emotions Research Center and the Asia Triple Helix Society, which was renamed WATEF in 2015. The journal has retained its title, ISSN and scholarly continuity throughout.

Editorial office

Cyber Emotions Research Center, Yeungnam University, 280 Daehak-Ro, Gyeongsan, Gyeongbuk 712-749, Republic of Korea — j.c.eastern.asia@gmail.com. The editors and their affiliations are listed on the Editorial Board page and the editorial office contacts are on the Contact page.

Indexing and preservation

JCEA is indexed in Scopus, EBSCOhost, Google Scholar and the Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ). Content is preserved long term by NDSL/KISTI and hosted on KoreaScience. See Abstracting, Indexing and Preservation and Archiving and Digital Preservation.

Policies

pages.title: Abstracting, Indexing and Preservation
pages.html:
Make your research known. Articles published in the Journal of Contemporary Eastern Asia are indexed and abstracted in the services below, so that peer-reviewed scholarship on East Asia, data and the networked society reaches a broad international audience.

Indexing and abstracting services

  • Scopus
  • EBSCOhost
  • Google Scholar
  • DOAJ — Directory of Open Access Journals
  • KoreaScience (KISTI)

Persistent identifiers

Every article is registered with a DOI under the prefix 10.17477, and article metadata — titles, authors, affiliations, abstracts, references and licence — is deposited with the registration agency and distributed to the indexing services listed above.

Digital preservation

The complete content of the journal is preserved for the long term by NDSL, the national scholarly-information archive of the Korea Institute of Science and Technology Information (KISTI), independently of the journal and its publishers. Full details of the journal's preservation arrangements, including what happens to the content should the journal cease to publish, are on the Archiving and Digital Preservation page.

pages.title: Call for Papers: Living with ChatGPT (Special Issue)
pages.html:
Call for Papers — Special Issue

Living with ChatGPT: Social, Psychological, and Economic Impacts of Generative AI in East Asia

Guest Editors: Dr. Weiwen Yu (Arizona State University) and Dr. Chun Shao (Marquette University)

This special issue examines how generative AI tools have transformed technology engagement, particularly following ChatGPT's release in 2022. It focuses on East Asian contexts, including China's regulatory environment, Japan's emphasis on human–machine harmony, and South Korea's digital labor markets.

Download the full call for papers (PDF)

Topics of Interest

  • AI in educational settings and academic integrity
  • Generative AI within creative industries
  • Language, translation, and cultural considerations in AI output
  • Economic effects including automation and labor changes
  • AI-assisted emotional support and social applications
  • Public perception and regulatory discussions
  • User adaptation and creative uses of AI tools
  • Regional adoption variations across East Asia

How to Submit

Send abstracts (maximum 500 words) to both Dr. Yu (weiwenyu@asu.edu) and Dr. Shao (chun.shao@marquette.edu), copying j.c.eastern.asia@gmail.com. Include “JCEA Special Issue” in the subject line.

Timeline

  • Abstract deadline: November 30, 2025
  • Full paper invitations: December 15, 2025
  • Manuscript deadline: May 15, 2026

Publication Fees

USD 100 standard APC; an additional USD 200 applies for funded research. Associate editors receive one annual exemption for unfunded work. Full details of the article processing charge, the exemptions and the journal's business model are on the Author Fees, Waivers and Business Model page.

pages.title: 2026 JCEA Summer Workshop: The Triple Helix, Socio-Technical Convergence, and New Asian Studies
pages.html:
This workshop explores the future of Asia through the convergence of Triple Helix collaboration — centred on universities, industry and government — with digital technology, networked societies and sociocultural change.

It approaches innovation not merely as a matter of science, technology or industrial development, but as a process through which universities, research institutions, industry, government and civil society jointly build a sustainable and resilient future. Through this, the workshop seeks to expand the research on Asian politics, society and economics accumulated by JCEA into the realms of socio-technical convergence, data and network societies, and future studies, while exploring a new academic agenda that connects the research capabilities of WATEF and the Cyber Emotions Research Center at Yeungnam University.
